source_text:
Στίχ. κε΄. Ἐκεῖ ἔθετο αὐτῷ ὁ Θεὸς δικαώματα καὶ κρίσεις, καὶ ἐκεῖ αὐτὸν ἐπείραζε.
Ἐπʼ ὠφελείᾳ πειράζει ὁ Θεός. Ἀπείραστος γάρ κακῶν. Ἀλλὰ διὰ τοῦτο πειράζει, ἵνα ἐὰν ὑπακούσωσιν αὐτῷ, τύχωσιν ἀγαθῶν, καὶ ἀπαλλα γῶσι κακῶν.
orientation: Origen begins his commentary on Exodus 15:25, explaining why God tested Israel at the place where he gave them ordinances and judgments.
pass_a_gloss: Verse 25. There God set for him ordinances and judgments, and there he was testing him. For benefit God tests. For he is untested by evils. But for this reason he tests, in order that if they obey him, they may obtain good things, and may be delivered from evils.

choices.why: Fixed glossary term for the statutes God gave at the place of testing.
Fixed glossary term paired with ordinances in the source.
Imperfect tense shows ongoing or repeated testing at that place; glossary root 'tests' retained.

choices.english: For he is untested by evils
choices.why: Keeps the passive sense of the adjective with genitive of thing; God has no experience of evils, so his testing cannot be harmful.
rejected: For he is without experience of evil
For he is untempted by evils

choices.why: Passive subjunctive of ἀπαλλάσσω with genitive of separation; keeps the purpose clause force after ἵνα.

bible_refs.note: Ἐκεῖ ἔθετο αὐτῷ ὁ Θεὸς δικαώματα καὶ κρίσεις, καὶ ἐκεῖ αὐτὸν ἐπείραζε

pass_b_english: There God set ordinances and judgments for him, and there he was testing him (Exodus 15:25). God tests for our benefit. For he is untested by evils. But he tests for this reason: so that if they obey him, they may obtain good things and be delivered from evils.
